Pianist Daniel Anastasio to perform free concert at Central Washington University
Pianist Daniel Anastasio will give a free concert at Central Washington University on October 14. The interactive event explores how different layers of music evoke emotion and features collaborations with faculty.
The Central Washington University Piano Club announced on Oct. 7 that pianist Daniel Anastasio will perform a free concert at the CWU Recital Hall on Wednesday, October 14, at 6 p.m.
The event, titled How Music’s Hidden Layers Guide Our Emotions, will take place in the McIntyre Music Building and feature an interactive performance designed to explore the underlying elements of music. The program aims to guide the audience through what lies beneath the surface of great musical works.
Anastasio's performance will include a special four-hands piece with Yerin Kim, Associate Professor of Piano at CWU. Through both playing and speaking, Anastasio will demonstrate how melody, harmony, bass lines, rhythm, and musical structure combine to create emotional impact in music. The program promises familiar masterpieces presented from new perspectives as well as lesser-known works.
The repertoire for October 14 includes compositions by J.S. Bach, Ludwig van Beethoven, Franz Schubert, Johannes Brahms, Edvard Grieg, Claude Debussy, Martin Bresnick, and others. Organizers say audiences from all backgrounds are invited to listen with fresh ears and engage in discovering connections within music.
Anastasio is based in San Antonio and is recognized as both a soloist and chamber musician. He serves as Artistic Director for organizations such as Agarita and the San Antonio Chamber Music Society; his programs have featured collaborations across artistic disciplines including dance and visual arts.
